Sale listings from realestate.com.au: houses and units for sale on REA, excluding those under offer, as recorded each month for the Demand Score in the Analytics Hub (Jan 2025 on). Each figure is the number of properties on the site on the day it was recorded, so it is close to, but not the same as, Cotality’s count of everything advertised during the month. Units are REA’s combined count (retirement, townhouse, unit, apartment, villa and house) minus houses. REA’s Brisbane covers a narrower area than Greater Brisbane, so its share of population reads low. Rental listings, days on market and population are still Cotality and ABS. The hub also holds Aug–Oct 2026, after the last Cotality month shown here.

Before Aug 2018: sale and rental listing data are not reliable for this earlier period. Cotality was still building its listings coverage, so early counts are understated, rental listings most of all; before about 2006 many markets have no rental count at all, so the all-markets line covers only the markets reporting each month (hover to see how many).

Is demand leaving, or shifting to renting?

Sale stock and rental stock on market, each traced over the last 12 months. If both are rising, demand is leaving the market. If sale stock is rising while rental stock falls, the demand is still there but has moved to renting.

How the demand reading is built

Sale stock on market. Cotality Market Trends, “# of listings last 1 months”: every property advertised for sale during the month, including ones still on the market from earlier months. Capitals use Greater Capital City areas; the 28 regional markets use their council area.

Controls. The bar at the top of the page sets the market, dwellings and sale-listings source for this section too. Range does not apply here: the reading always uses the last 12 monthly counts. With the top market on All 36 markets, the detail shows the last market picked.

realestate.com.au. With Sale listings set to realestate.com.au at the top of the page, the sale side uses REA’s monthly counts from the Analytics Hub instead (houses, and REA’s combined count minus houses for units). The rental side, vacancy rate and the 12-month window stay the same, so the two readings can be compared market by market. REA’s Brisbane covers a narrower area than Greater Brisbane.

Rental stock on market. The rental listings count behind Cotality’s 1-month vacancy rate. Cotality publishes the rate, not the count, but the rate is stored as an exact fraction (rental listings ÷ rental stock), so both numbers can be recovered. In Townsville, Jul 2026, RP Data’s own rental count agrees within about 7%. The vacancy rate shown is the same count ÷ rental stock.

The trend. A straight-line trend fitted through the last 12 monthly counts (on a log scale, so a market of any size reads in percent), expressed as the change from the start of the trend line to its end. It uses every month in the window rather than just the first and last, so one unusual month moves it less. The 12 months run winter to winter, so the seasonal dip over summer and rise into spring roughly balance out, but a market with a strong seasonal swing can still lean one way. A trend within ±5% is marked borderline: the reading follows the direction, but the move is small.

The four readings. Sale up, rent up: demand leaving. Sale up, rent down: demand shifting to renting (people still arriving but not buying). Sale down, rent up: demand shifting from renting to buying. Sale down, rent down: tightening on both sides.

Population. ABS Regional Population to 30 June 2025 is the latest available, so the population figure shown is growth over 2024–25. It gives context for whether people are still arriving; it does not cover the 12 months shown.

Houses and units. Cotality reassigned some properties between houses and units in Nov 2024 and Jan 2026. Totals for all dwellings are unaffected; the split is not.

How this is built, and what to watch for

Listings. Cotality Market Trends, one workbook per month, Aug 2018 to Jul 2026. Sale listings before that come from Cotality’s older monthly history files (see Earlier years). Both lines are monthly counts: sale listings are Cotality’s “# of listings last 1 months”, and rental listings are recovered from Cotality’s vacancy rate (see Monthly figures). Capitals use Cotality’s capital-city rows (Greater Capital City areas). The 28 regional markets use their council (LGA) rows, the same split the Traffic Lights tool uses.

Monthly figures. Sale listings are Cotality’s published 1-month count (“# of listings last 1 months”): every property advertised for sale during the month. Cotality publishes no 1-month rental count as such, but its 1-month vacancy rate is stored as an exact fraction, rental listings ÷ rental stock, so the monthly rental line is that listings count, recovered from the rate (for example 0.0269896… = 39 ÷ 1,445). It is a real Cotality figure from Aug 2018, including Dec 2023 – Oct 2024 when the 12-month rental total is missing, and RP Data’s own count agrees within about 7% (Townsville, Jul 2026). Before Aug 2018 the count can’t be recovered reliably, so those months are an estimate (12-month total ÷ 12, shaped by the vacancy rate) scaled to meet the real count at Aug 2018. The two lines are not on the same basis. The sale count includes properties still on the market from earlier months, about 25–27% of its 12-month total; rentals lease faster and the rental count runs at about 7% of its 12-month total. Read each line for its direction and timing, not for the gap between them.

realestate.com.au option. Sale listings can be switched to realestate.com.au. The counts are the ones recorded each month for the Demand Score in the Analytics Hub (houses for sale, and REA’s combined property-type count, both excluding listings under offer), from Jan 2025. Units are the combined count minus houses; Wodonga Dec 2025 is left out because its combined count is below its house count. REA has no 12-month total, so this option shows monthly figures only, and REA’s Brisbane covers a narrower area than Greater Brisbane. Rental listings stay on Cotality either way.

Population. ABS Regional Population 2024–25 (3218.0): Greater Capital City areas for the eight capitals and LGAs for the rest. Each 30 June figure matches the Traffic Lights tool exactly. Months between two June figures are interpolated in a straight line. Months after Jun 2025 (all of 2026 so far) use the Jun 2025 figure, the latest ABS estimate, until the ABS publishes 2025–26.

Count-method changes. A 12-month total can’t move 15% or more in a single month from real activity, so a jump that size is marked as a change in how Cotality counts. The big ones are Mar 2020 (capitals), May 2020 (rentals down about 23% everywhere) and Jan 2021 (rentals back up about 33%). Nov 2024 and Jan 2026 move listings between houses and units, which is why the All view is steadier than Houses or Units alone. Compare levels within a stretch between markers, not across one.

Earlier years. Jan 2001 to Jun 2018 come from Cotality’s older history files: the capital-city file and the ten LGA files. The old files count more listings than the monthly files at the same date, by different amounts in each market. For houses the old sale count runs from 5% lower (Newcastle) to 68% higher (Perth). So each market’s houses and units, sale and rental, are rescaled separately, so that Jun 2018 meets the Aug 2018 level, and that scale is held for every earlier month. Both lines are drawn lighter before Aug 2018. Switch Before Aug 2018 to As published to see the older files’ own figures without rescaling; the lines then step at Aug 2018.

Early rental listings are understated. Cotality’s rental coverage kept growing until about 2016. Capitals’ rental listings went from 1.5% of population in 2008 to 3.7% in 2016 before levelling off, which is far more than the rental market itself moved. Some regional markets barely register before 2010 (Launceston houses: 7 rental listings a year in 2008). Treat the rental line before about 2016 as showing direction only, not level. Sale listing coverage settled around 2008: regional sale listings more than doubled from 2004 to 2008, then flattened. The chart can go back to Jan 2001 at most, because that is where the ABS population estimates start (30 June 2001, held for Jan–May 2001). Before about 2006 many markets have no rental count, and some none for sale (Launceston has no sale count until Feb 2008). The All 36 markets line therefore adds up only the markets reporting each month and divides by those markets’ population, so a missing market drops out of both sides. The mix of markets changes as each one starts reporting; the hover note gives the count for each month.

Jul 2018. The month Cotality switched council boundaries. Merged councils are missing (Central Coast shows 423 sale listings), and the older files end in Jun 2018, so the month is left empty.

Sale and rental listings chart. One bar for sale listings and one for rental listings each month, as counts: the same figures the line chart divides by population. Each bar is the total for the dwellings chosen: with All, houses (darker) and units (lighter) are stacked; with Units alone the bars take the lighter shades.

Overlays. The tick boxes on the sale listings chart add days on market, cash rate, Bank Rate and vacancy rate. Days on market has its own right-hand axis; the three rates share a % axis beyond it. Both rates come from the RBA. Cash rate is the cash rate target at month end, drawn as steps (table F1; before 2011 the RBA file holds monthly averages, so a month with a change takes the new rate). Bank Rate (from mid-2004, when the RBA series starts) is the banks’ discounted variable rate for owner-occupier housing loans (table F5, indicator lending rates). It sits close to what new borrowers actually pay; the standard variable rate runs about 2 points higher. Both read off the right-hand % axis.

Vacancy rate (sale listings chart). Tick Vacancy rate on the sale listings chart to add Cotality’s 1-month vacancy rate (rental listings ÷ rental stock), one line for houses (solid) and one for units (dashed), or just the one chosen under Dwellings, on the % axis it shares with the interest rates. Markets are combined by rental stock, and only markets reporting that month are included. It is drawn lighter before Aug 2018, when Cotality’s rental counts were still incomplete, so early vacancy reads low. It is always Cotality, whichever sale-listings source is chosen.
